added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs: the node's done-when fences the head arm at the three SPA/route test files plus the serve.py module bound and delegates the server-importer population to the coordinator's merge run (prompt.txt FENCE-EVIDENCE), so the after arm is the readable one: after_suite 27 passed, EXIT=0 at c8b8fd834 (logs/gate.log, revision header c8b8fd834efa0660aa3410732206156f33a75937, summary line '27 passed in 43.22s'); the reviewed manifest records no separately run baseline_suite and explains that the base arm was not run, so there is no baseline failing-id set to fall back on; after minus base failure ids is empty either way because the after arm records zero failures.

findings.text: follow-on: the runs handed to scheduleFetchDue are the fleet-wide list, not this project's: shell.jsx:319 reads payload.runs from the project-less /crew poll (reckon/serve.py:3039 answers _crew_rows(mounts, None), which selects every mount at serve.py:764), while the schedule fetched is window.STATE.project's alone (shell.jsx:321), and scheduleRunSignature keys each run by its project (docs/ui/state-loader.js:288-296). A run whose phase moves in any other mounted project therefore changes the signature and spends a /_schedule/<this project> request on a schedule that has not changed. The drawn flow is unaffected and s11's budget (one per minute of the crew view being open plus one per run-phase change the poll saw, prompt.txt FENCE-EVIDENCE) still holds because the poll did see the change, so this is a request cost on a busy fleet rather than a gate failure; narrowing the due test to the project's own runs (or hoisting the filter the crew view already applies) would remove it.

follow-on: the new failure branch is unexercised. state-loader.js:331-334 keeps the schedule already on screen and marks it stale with the route's error when the route answers 200 without a schedule, but every case that drives refreshSchedule serves a schedule: _SCHEDULE_ANSWERS at tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py:378 answers ok({project, schedule: DATA.schedule_route}) on every /_schedule/sample call, and tests/test_the_flow_refreshes_from_its_own_route.py:211 covers the server half of the same rule (a null schedule beside schedule_error) only. A regression that dropped the stale marking, or the payload.schedule_error guard, would leave the suite green, and s11's done-when asks the replacement to hold 'under the stale rule' (prompt.txt FENCE the schedule replaces window.STATE.schedule under the stale rule). One loader case answering {schedule: null, schedule_error: '...'} while a schedule is held would close it.

item_verdicts.manifest: Read; status complete, four commits named (457cdbe4e, 140ce22d7, b9856d7ea, c8b8fd834), after_suite recorded as 27 passed EXIT=0 at c8b8fd834, negative_control_log given as a bare path (logs/negative-control.log), and two unmeasured things stated rather than hidden: the base arm unrun and docs/ui/crew.jsx untouched.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The manifest declares nine write paths (reckon/serve.py, docs/ui/state-loader.js, docs/ui/shell.jsx, docs/ui/crew.jsx, the three test files, the evidence fragment and the figures directory); git diff --stat 307e0adf8..c8b8fd834 changes exactly seven of them and nothing else, with docs/ui/crew.jsx and docs/figures/... left untouched.

justifications.durability: The change is guarded by cases that are shown to fire, not merely to pass: the declared control at logs/apply_negative_control.py:49 is six anchor-pair mutations applied as one edit set and reversed from a trap, and logs/negative-control.log records 8 failed against the head arm's 27 passing with EXIT=1 and REVERSE_EXIT=0. The assertions are independent of the values under test: tests/test_the_flow_refreshes_from_its_own_rule` no. tests/test_the_flow_refreshes_from_its_own_route.py:171 asserts _split_instant(first) == INSTANT_ONE where the left side is reference+split read back off the served payload and the right is the instant the frozen clock was handed, and mutation 5 (serve the first request's build to every later one) reddens both anchor cases; tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py:1546 asserts observed['replaced'] against the stub payload and would fail if refreshSchedule stopped assigning state.schedule, and the case as a whole is falsified by mutation 2, though no mutation falsifies that single line on its own — the stronger companions are served_reference (an independent literal) and held_reference != served_reference at :1547-1549. The deduction: the loader's failure branch, which marks the held schedule stale with the route's error (docs/ui/state-loader.js:331-334), is exercised by no case, so a regression that dropped it would leave the suite green.
justifications.evidence: The gate is a real measurement of the done-when and its result is recorded rather than claimed: logs/gate.log ends 27 passed / EXIT=0 at a header naming c8b8fd834 over exactly the four files the done-when fences, logs/browser-probe.log records the two browser cases passing, and logs/negative-control.log records 8 failed / 19 passed with EXIT=1 and REVERSE_EXIT=0 plus an empty post-reverse git status. The deduction: the base arm is genuinely unrun, so the delta evidence is the control set rather than an absolute count against base; the manifest discloses this and the node's own done-when delegates the server-importer population to the coordinator's merge, so the absence is bounded rather than concealed.
justifications.fit: The addition follows the module it lands in: the route sits beside its siblings in the same do_GET dispatch and is documented the way they are (reckon/serve.py:3321-3333), the loader helpers are named by mechanism (scheduleRunSignature, scheduleFetchDue, refreshSchedule), and the shell reuses the existing startPoll rather than a second poll effect. The four commits carry conventional subjects with substantive bodies and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier (457cdbe4e 'feat(crew): refresh the schedule from its own route on the crew poll' body explains the fleet-event cost), no AI trailer appears in any of them, and a scan of the changed paths finds no phase/plan label in a symbol, filename or comment.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Every half of the goal is landed: reckon/serve.py:3321-3360 answers GET /_schedule/<project> from route_results._served_result(('discover', project)) plus _attach_schedule_for_read (serve.py:3342) so the schedule is rebuilt per request at reference=datetime.now(UTC); docs/ui/shell.jsx:322 asks for it from the crew poll; and docs/ui/state-loader.js:858-867 no longer calls refetchDerived on a fleet event while :849 still does on a change, so the fleet event now only republishes its key.
justifications.reuse: The route does not fork an existing capability, it extends the owner of the schedule capability: the server side calls _attach_schedule_for_read (reckon/serve.py:1778), the same helper /_discover uses at :3374, and adds no second schedule builder. A capability search for a schedule-only read over reckon/ and a poll-driven derived refetch over docs/ui/ found none — docs/ui/state-loader.js already had watchProjectStateChanges' change-driven refetchDerived (:827), which fetches the whole page payload and is a different capability, and the shell's poll already existed (docs/ui/_shared.jsx:11, shell.jsx:316) and is reused rather than reimplemented; the stale marking the new fetch keeps (:331) is a re-issue of the discovery path's own rule at :526, which docs/ui/crew.jsx:87-92 already renders.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 307e0adf8..c8b8fd834 touches only docs/ui/shell.jsx, docs/ui/state-loader.js, reckon/serve.py, tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py, tests/test_spa_derived_flow.py, tests/test_the_flow_refreshes_from_its_own_route.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-page-paints-from-an-index/the-flow-refreshes-from-its-own-route.html, every one of them inside the nine declared write paths (prompt.txt FENCE-SCOPE); the declared docs/ui/crew.jsx and docs/figures/... are untouched, and no plan, index or sprint state appears in the diff.
